text:
MPC edged up 0.44% today, holding near its recent highs after a sharp rally over the past week. The stock has recovered $42 from its November 6 low, driven largely by refinery economics: US oil prices sitting at $89.62 per barrel and refineries running at 95.2% capacity create strong conditions for fuel margins. Heating oil prices up 59% year-over-year adds tailwind—high distillate demand supports the refining business, even as it squeezes consumers paying the bills.

The broader context, though, has shifted. News that Russian crude production has rebounded and global oil markets are returning to surplus (supply exceeding demand) could eventually pressure oil prices and refining margins downward. For now, tight refinery utilization and elevated heating oil needs are keeping the stock supported, but this surplus signal suggests the favorable refining environment may not last indefinitely.
